en.p: In the coordinate plane, for the three points $\mathrm{A}(-3,\,1)$, $\mathrm{B}(0,\,2)$, $\mathrm{C}(1,\,0)$, two points P, Q satisfy

Let $\mathrm{P_0}$, $\mathrm{Q_0}$ be the two points P, Q, respectively, at which the value of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AP}}\cdot\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AQ}}$ is minimal. For a point X on segment $\mathrm{AP_0}$ with $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{BX}}\cdot\overrightarrow{\mathrm{BQ_0}}\ge 1$, the maximum value of $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{Q_0X}}|^2$ is $\dfrac{q}{p}$. Find the value of $p+q$. (Here O is the origin, and $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
